title: Who is who in Deep Water
back: Douglas (narrator), the eighteen-year-old bully (never named), the instructor (belt, breathing, kicking, combine).

title: Deep Water in six beats
back: Beach → pool → three attempts → years of terror → instructor's method → self-tests and the lesson about fear.

title: The first wave
back: The waves knocked him down and buried him; his breath was gone; his father laughed. A small seed of fear — the first of the two incidents examiners ask about.

back: An eighteen-year-old picked him up and tossed him in; he landed sitting, swallowed water and sank. Nine feet seemed like ninety.

back: First: jump off the bottom, yellowish water, grab at nothing. Second: paralysed legs, no scream. Third: effort stops, drowsy peace, darkness. Revived vomiting by the pool.

title: Only the fear of death
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Roosevelt's line, Douglas's life" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><circle cx="160" cy="90" r="60" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="8"/><text x="160" y="96" text-anchor="middle" font-size="22" font-weight="700" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none">fear</text><text x="160" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.8" stroke="none">the only thing we have to fear is fear itself</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Roosevelt's line, Douglas's life</text></svg>
back: In the face of death he felt terror and then peace, so death did not frighten him — only its fear did. Conquering it set him free to live intensely.
